scope_entries.finding: SQLite schema: the items table has kind CHECK('book','article'). The devices table already has a firmware_version column. There is no firmware table and no per-device target version, and the store has no migration path beyond CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS.

Protocol v1 has the endpoints status, queue, items/{id} and ack. Every status field is optional. firmware_version is stored and displayed but nothing acts on it. There is no OTA endpoint. Changes must be additive, or they need a new protocol version (device-protocol.md:4-5). A 426 already means 'firmware update needed'.
The privacy gate proves zero egress, and scan-secrets rejects non-localhost URLs in tracked JSON. A server-side OTA source therefore has to be upload-only, and the fake device needs an OTA leg.

OTA already exists. Today it checks GitHub releases/latest for agentculture/xteink-firmware (OtaUpdater.cpp:25-32). It parses the release JSON, streams the image over wolfSSL HttpDownloader into esp_ota_write, and compares versions with isUpdateNewer, which accepts X.Y.Z only. The UI is under Settings. The source URL is hard-wired.

ota_0 and ota_1 are 6,553,600 B each, and otadata is present. The app is 5.89 MB, so about 10% of each slot is free. Changing partitions would need a factory flash, which wipes NVS provisioning (x3-flash-protocol memory).

CONFIG_BOOTLOADER_APP_ROLLBACK_ENABLE=y, but initArduino marks every booted app valid unless verifyRollbackLater() is overridden, and nothing in src/, lib/ or freeink-sdk overrides it. Today rollback therefore only catches an image that crashes before init. Secure boot and signed apps are off (sdkconfig.defaults:400-402).

SNTP (HalClock::syncFromNTP, TrustedTime) and the TZ picker exist, and Jerusalem is in the table. TrustedTime.h:6-8 says the C3 keeps time through deep sleep but loses it on power-off, and that there is no battery-backed RTC. An I2C RTC capability is compiled for X3 (BoardConfig.h:302). The xteink/d2-nav-sntp branch is already merged into feat/issue-1.

sync::run(renderer*, Callbacks{}, budget) already runs headless (onStationJoined at :831). It does LAN first with a 4 s timeout, then the tunnel, with a 60 s item budget. Results are written to NVS sync_last and drawn on Home only when Home repaints. Wi-Fi activities reboot for a fresh heap first, because there is only about 50 KB free while reading and TLS peaks around 39 KB.

A headless join of the last-connected SSID already exists: WiFi.begin with a 10 s deadline, gated at 20% battery, and it starts TrustedTime when connected. This is the template for the scheduled join.

The CLI nouns are device, library, server, tunnel and mcp. device has list, queue, revoke and overview (device.py:117-141). There are 3 MCP tools: push_file, list_library and send_to_device. DevicesView.tsx:207-210 already shows Firmware when firmware_version is set, and api.ts:44 already has it on the Device type. Nothing for schedules or firmware exists anywhere.

The CI guard pins the OTA source away from upstream and bans setInsecure in the OTA/TLS files. CONTRIBUTING says updates come from the fork's releases, never upstream's. That rule and docs/xteink/tls.md:212-228 (the OTA source section) need rewording for a server source.

kind='article' is only a label: Markdown/HTML uploads default to it (ingest.py:171). Every item is pushed by the web UI, the CLI or MCP. There is no RSS, URL fetch or scheduled ingest, and there are no server background tasks (only the dual uvicorn asyncio.gather in app.py:188).
Both issue-1 PRs are OPEN. main holds only the scaffold, so the server, protocol and sync client exist only on the feat/issue-1 branches.

Sleep on Xteink C3 boards drives GPIO13 low, which cuts power to the battery MOSFET, then runs esp_deep_sleep_start. The only armed wake source is the power-button GPIO. esp_sleep_enable_timer_wakeup is used nowhere, and HalGPIO::getWakeupReason (HalGPIO.cpp:246-267) has no Timer case. On battery a timer wake is impossible without changing the power-off design; on USB the chip stays in deep sleep.

The LAN URL may be plain http (TlsTrust.h:15-17); the tunnel requires a pinned CA bundle (XteinkCaBundle.h) plus hostname verification. The GitHub roots in the bundle exist for OTA (tls.md:60). There is no image signing anywhere.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / lifecycle lens: memory issue1-handoff-state (X3 runs eab86526) + OtaUpdater.cpp:25-32
scope_entries.finding: Bootstrap: there is a chicken-and-egg step. The device can't OTA into the OTA feature.

scope_entries.surface: challenge pass / concurrency lens: xteink/core/store.py + routes_device.py
scope_entries.finding: Clean pass. There is one device per key and a single sqlite writer per request. A firmware download beside a book download in the same run is sequential on the device. Residual: two devices fetching the same image at once is plain read concurrency on a content-addressed blob, so there's no new hazard.

Clean pass. An interrupted download or power loss mid-write leaves the running slot untouched (begin erases only the inactive slot, and the boot partition switches only after end plus verify). It retries the next day. Residual: no Range resume into an OTA slot, so a flaky link re-downloads the whole 5.9 MB.
